records.label: Think and Discuss
records.quote: Which of these relations satifies the following condition: each
records.text: Which of these relations satifies the following condition: each element of X is connected to only one element of Y.

records.quote: A relation from X to Y is said to be a function if:
records.claim: A relation from X to Y is a function if each of the elements of X appears only once as a first projection in one of the ordered pairs of the relation.

records.quote: The Symbolic representation of the function:
records.text: The Symbolic representation of the function:

records.quote: The function is denoted by one of the following symbols: f or m
records.claim: A function is denoted by one of the symbols f, m, Q, ...; the function f from the set X to the set Y is written $f : X \to Y$ and read "f is a function from X to Y".

records.quote: Notes:
If f is a function from X to itself, we say that f is a function on X.
records.claim: If f is a function from X to itself, f is called a function on X.

records.quote: If the ordered pair (x, y) belongs to the function, then the element
records.claim: If the ordered pair (x, y) belongs to the function, y is called the image of x by f, expressed as $f : x \mapsto y$ (read: the function f maps x to y) or $f(x) = y$ (read: f is a function where f(x) = y).

records.quote: The Domain, the codomain and the range
records.text: The Domain, the codomain and the range

records.quote: If f is a function from X to Y.
records.text: If f is a function from X to Y, i.e. $f: X \to Y$, then

records.quote: The set X is called the domain of the function f.
records.claim: The set X is called the domain of the function f.

records.quote: The set Y is called the codomain of the function f.
records.claim: The set Y is called the codomain of the function f.

records.quote: The set of images of the elements of the domain of X
records.claim: The set of images of the elements of the domain X by the function f is called the range of the function.

records.label: For example
solution: The domain of the function f is the set $X=\{-1,2,3\}$
The codomain of the function f is the set $Y=\{2,3,5,7\}$
The range of the function f is the set of the images of the elements of X by the function f and equal to $\{3,5,7\}$
records.notes: Stem begins with a stray comma before X in print.

records.quote: X Y arrow diagram -1, 2, 3 to 2, 3, 5, 7
records.caption: Arrow diagram from X = {-1, 2, 3} to Y = {2, 3, 5, 7}: -1→3, 2→7, 3→5.

records.quote: Note that: The range is a subset of the codomain of the function.
records.claim: The range is a subset of the codomain of the function.

records.label: Example
records.stem: If $X=\{2,3,4\}$, $Y=\{y : y\in N, 2\le y<9\}$ where N is the set of natural numbers, and R is a relation from X to Y where a R b means: « $a=\frac{1}{2}b$» for each of $a\in X$, $b\in Y$, write R and represent it by an arrow diagram show that R is a function from X to Y and find its range.
solution: R is a function because every element of the X has only one arrow coming out to one element of Y.
records.notes: Printed 'a R b' and 'show that' without punctuation; recorded as printed.

objectives.label: Decide whether a relation is a function
objectives.description: Decide whether a relation from X to Y is a function, from its ordered pairs, arrow diagram or cartesian diagram, by checking that each element of X has exactly one image.

objectives.label: Use function notation
objectives.description: Write a function symbolically as f: X → Y, f: x ↦ y or f(x) = y, and name the image of an element.

objectives.label: Represent a function by diagrams
objectives.description: Represent a relation or function by ordered pairs, an arrow diagram and a cartesian diagram.

objectives.label: Find the domain, codomain and range
objectives.description: Find the domain, codomain and range of a function, and recognise that the range is a subset of the codomain.
